_authority: Machine-readable description of the NOVIKONTAS tablet platform AS IT IS, discovered 2026-09-08 by inspection of the Android project and the live course. The scripts read this file; SKILL.md and the references must not restate its paths in prose. When the platform changes, change this file - not the scripts.
_related: course-factory/knowledge/delivery-contract.json is the authority on how a course is BUILT and what shape it must have. This file describes how it is PUBLISHED and what the app looks like today. Where they overlap, delivery-contract.json wins on the target design and this file wins on present-day fact.

repository._path_note: There is no fixed path. Every colleague clones the platform repository somewhere different, so the scripts take --repo, and publish.py finds it by looking for a git repository whose origin URL matches remote_match - first from the working directory upwards, then in the usual places below.
repository._default_branch_note: DETECTED, not assumed. The remote's HEAD is `master`. Colleagues and prompts often say 'main'; the scripts detect it at run time and never hard-code either name.
repository._github_cli_note: `gh` is not installed on this machine and no GH token is in the environment, so a pull request cannot be opened by API. The publisher pushes the branch and prints the GitHub compare URL for a human to click. If `gh` is installed later, the flow does not change - only the last step gets automated.
repository._ci_note: No .github/workflows. Nothing validates on the server side, so the local gate IS the gate.

asset_roots._merge_note: Gradle merges the flavour source sets into ONE asset root at build time, so at runtime the two terminals are SIBLINGS. A cross-terminal link is written relative to that merged root and looks dead in the split source tree. Never 'fix' a link without checking it against a merged view (course-factory/tablet/scripts/verify_links.py builds one).

flavours._separation: The role separation is STRUCTURAL and this is the whole reason it holds: the trainee flavour never packages src/instructor/assets, so instructor material cannot reach a trainee tablet by accident. The one thing that defeats it is an instructor-only FILE placed inside the trainee tree by hand - which is exactly what the roles gate looks for.

pack.status: target - use for every NEW course
pack.manifest: course.json at the trainee pack root
pack.why: One folder per course means two colleagues publishing two courses touch no file in common. It is also what course-factory/knowledge/delivery-contract.json already specifies.

legacy.status: GAS BASIC only - do not create another
legacy.why: GAS BASIC predates the pack layout. Its files sit directly at the terminal roots with no course segment in any path, so a second course cannot use the same locations. Converting it is a separate, human-authorised job: it moves ~400 files and every relative link with them.

gas-basic.title: GAS BASIC
gas-basic.note: The whole of both terminals IS this course today. That is why publishing it stages the entire terminal tree, and why a second course must not be added in this layout.

course_identity_surface._what: Where a course name was baked into code. As of 2026-09-09 the SHELLS read it from data: gb_config.js (COURSE, COURSE_ID, RUN_CODE) is the one place a build names its course, courses/registry.js (generated by this skill's registry.py) lists the courses the APK holds, it_auth.js derives INSTALLED from it, and gb_nav/it_nav/radar/record/run read the title from GB_CONFIG. What still needs a human when a SECOND course pack is added is listed in `still_manual`.

role_rules._shared_note: Shared engines live ONCE at the terminal root and are referenced, never copied into a course. A copy goes stale the first time the engine is fixed - that has already happened here: the per-module gb_done.js exists in five identical copies.
instructor_only_filename_patterns: the instructor's analysis of a case
the printable paper check, whose last page is the marking key
role_rules._content_pattern_note: Filename patterns are reliable and FAIL. CONTENT patterns are signals, not proof, so they WARN: on this platform every broad content match turned out to be prose - 'Answer keys trace to: SIGTTO...' is a provenance line, 'one instructor only' is a staffing note. The scanner also strips HTML and JavaScript comments first, because a comment citing the answer key as a source is not a leak.
instructor_only_content_patterns: the page carries an INSTRUCTOR ONLY banner
an answer-key heading or link label
an instruction not to issue the document to trainees
an assessor signature block - this is a marking form

trainee_allowlist.reason: a cargo record FORM the trainee reads as reference material; 'record' in the name is the ship's record, not an assessor's
the ship/shore safety checklist is a real operational document the trainee must be able to read
a trainee task ABOUT the checklist
the trainee's own result sheet prints a line for the assessor to sign so the paper record can be completed in the room; the marking criteria and key themselves live on the instructor terminal

role_rules._internal_note: REVIEW.html is the PREVIEW surface the colleague reads in a browser. It is generated beside the course, is not course content, and must never reach a tablet - so it is internal by pattern rather than by anyone remembering to delete it.

patterns: a Supabase SERVICE-ROLE key bypasses row-level security entirely
a JWT. A Supabase ANON key here is publishable by design; anything else is not - decode it and check the 'role' claim
secrets._anon_key_note: gb_config.js carries the Supabase ANON key. That key is designed to be shipped in a client and is not a leak. Its safety rests entirely on row-level security being correct in backend/ - the tablets make unauthenticated writes to course_runs and unlocks, so anyone who unzips the APK can reach those endpoints. An RLS audit is worth doing; it is not this gate's job.

offline._rule: A remote SCRIPT or a remote STYLESHEET the page needs in order to be readable is a FAIL: a classroom may have no network. A remote FONT whose stacks end in a generic family is a WARN, because the degradation is a chosen fallback rather than a broken page.
offline._known_gap: GAS BASIC pulls Raleway from Google Fonts on ~105 pages with no bundled copy. Every stack ends in a generic family, so it degrades gracefully and the brand typeface is lost offline. This is why fonts warn instead of failing - a FAIL here would block every publication of the working course.

addresses._note: Only the local_live pages may name a laptop address, and there they are placeholder text in a field the instructor types into. Those pages are packaged only by the traineeLocal/instructorLocal TEST flavours.

rights._note: _figure_meta.json carries a RIGHTS field per figure, and some ICS figures are marked 'NOT cleared for issue or publication'. Pushing those to a shared repository is a distribution decision. The gate names them and lets a human decide; it does not block, because the repository is private and the figures are already in the APK.

validation._order: Run the publisher's own gate first (it is fast and catches the dangerous things), then the course-factory checks, which know about decks and hours.

external_scripts._root_note: course-factory sits BESIDE this skill - both as user skills in ~/.claude/skills/ and inside a plugin's skills/ folder - so the scripts resolve it as a sibling of the skill directory. Nothing here is an absolute path.

it_run.js.rule: GENERATED - never hand-edited, and regenerated after ANY deck change. A stale slide number lies silently: the instructor announces the wrong task and finds out in the room.

courses/registry.js.rule: GENERATED by scanning courses/*/course.json. Deterministic and sorted, so two colleagues who both regenerate it produce the same bytes and a textual conflict is resolved by re-running the generator, never by hand-merging.

packaging_note: There is no working automated copy from the authoring course folder into the Android assets. build_tablet_package.py exists in the course's working area but its own output file (gb_tasks.js) carries a warning that running it would revert hand-made corrections. Treat the Android project as the source of truth for what ships, and the course folder as the source of truth for what the course SAYS.
